verdict.rationale: Mastra's docs say you run the Mastra server locally and can ship agents and workflows as standalone endpoints inside your own Node.js apps, so the core product runs on user infrastructure. The evidence lacks dedicated self-hosted production deployment documentation, and a community report says the Elastic v2 license forbids offering the software as a hosted or managed service. missing for 10: explicit self-hosted production deployment docs (e.g. own server or container), self-hosting parity for Studio and observability versus Mastra Cloud, independent hands-on self-hosting reports, clarity on license restrictions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Register agents and workflows on one Mastra server, run it locally, and deploy the same app to Mastra Cloud.
Mastra bundles agents and workflows directly into existing React, Next.js and Node.js apps, or ships them as standalone endpoints.
Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license, which forbids providing the software as a hosted or managed service.
